items.title: The 17 SDGs replaced the 8 Millennium Development Goals in 2015
items.claim: What are the UN Sustainable Development Goals?

options.text: A binding international treaty signed by all nations
17 goals with 169 targets agreed by UN member states in September 2015, to be met by 2030 — covering poverty, education, climate, gender equality and others; non-binding but with national reporting

items.reveal:
The Millennium Development Goals (2000-2015, 8 goals, 21 targets) focused on poverty reduction in LICs. The SDGs (2015-2030, 17 goals, 169 targets) apply universally — HICs are also measured.

Progress is monitored through Voluntary National Reviews. The UN's annual SDG report tracks the 232 indicators. The COVID-19 pandemic reversed progress on several goals; the UN reports that the world is not on track for any of the 17 goals at projected 2030.

The SDGs replaced the MDGs partly because the latter were criticised for being designed by HICs for LICs without sufficient consultation.
items.why: The architecture of international development matters. Whether progress targets are set globally and how they are measured shapes national policy priorities — even when there is no enforcement mechanism.

items.title: Glaciers can move metres per day during surges

options.text: Typically tens to hundreds of metres per year for valley glaciers; outlet glaciers like Jakobshavn (Greenland) reached around 17 km/year (around 46 m/day) in 2012; surge-type glaciers (around 1% of all glaciers) can move metres per day for months
Always 1 mm per year, too slow to detect
All glaciers move at the same uniform rate

items.reveal:
Glacier flow combines internal deformation (creep — ice flowing under its own weight, around 10-100 m/year for valley glaciers) and basal sliding (much faster when meltwater lubricates the bed).

Jakobshavn Isbrae drains around 7% of the Greenland Ice Sheet; its mass loss has been measured by satellite altimetry and GRACE. Variegated Glacier (Alaska) surged at around 65 m/day in 1982-83.

Climate warming has accelerated many outlet glaciers in Greenland and Antarctica — ice shelves at the front buttress the ice behind; when shelves break up, the ice behind speeds up. Pine Island and Thwaites (Antarctica) are the major current concerns.
items.why: Glacier dynamics control sea-level contribution. Flow speeds and acceleration mechanisms are central uncertainties in projecting 21st-century sea-level rise.
